newsitem.title: UK: UK's ITV companies sign up for digital TV.
newsitem.headline: UK's ITV companies sign up for digital TV.

text.p: Britain's 15 Independent Television companies on Tuesday confirmed plans to launch a digital television service in 1998.
The companies will join with Channel Four in applying for the digital multiplex licence reserved for Britain's two commercial public service channels - Channel Four and ITV.
The ITV firms - which include Carlton Communications Plc and Granada Group Plc, are looking at plans for new national and regional services and expect to unveil these by the end of this year.

"Digital television will offer our viewers widescreen pictures and high quality sound, new TV channels and the prospect of interactive services as well," Leslie Hill, chairman of the ITV Association said in a statement.

Earlier the BBC said it would launch free-to-air digital terrestrial television services, taking a guaranteed place on a digital terrestrial multiplex, which are a bundle of digital channels, for the launch of digital terrestrial television.

There will be four other multiplexes which will be advertised and auctioned off next month by the Independent Television Commission. Licences for these should be granted next summer. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
